blocks.text: This chapter brings Absalom’s rebellion to its decisive end. Absalom had built support, declared himself king, and forced David from Jerusalem; here David’s forces defeat the rebellion. The outcome is personally tragic for David: although he had publicly ordered his commanders to deal gently with Absalom, Joab kills him.

Second Samuel traces David’s rise and the strengthening of his kingdom, but it also follows the damage of royal abuse, violence within his household, rebellion, and grief. Absalom’s death and David’s mourning belong within that larger movement of the book.
